confirmed_defect.evidence: The original gate constructs originals=dict(curves(baseline)) and immediately asserts len(originals)*150 == Parquet metadata num_rows. Default Python therefore rejects duplicate baseline identities. Under python -O that assertion, candidate uniqueness, missing-baseline and required-addition assertions are disabled. The dictionary retains only the last duplicate. pd.testing.assert_frame_equal remains active but checks only that retained observation. Earlier unconditional-acceptance claim was incorrect.
confirmed_defect.synthetic_counterexample: Persisted synthetic baseline A(value2), A(value1), 300 rows; candidate A(value1), B, 300 rows. Unchanged original verify_preserved AST rejects with AssertionError at optimize=0 and accepts at optimize=2 in a python -O subprocess. New gate raises ValueError in both default and optimized subprocesses. No actual GT21 data were read.

new_gate.scope: One bounded recording. Explicit errors remain active under -O. Stores baseline fingerprints only; max 25000 observations, 150 rows/observation, 8 MiB batch. Arrow wrapper requires exact schema metadata and input hashes unchanged. This is hardening against optimization-sensitive assertions, not evidence default queued pilots accepted duplicate baselines.
new_gate.validation: 16 tests passed in 2.75 seconds under a 768 MiB address-space cap with single-thread numerical libraries. Actual tiny Parquet row groups of 73 rows exercise 150-row batch assembly, metadata mismatch, partial observations, mixed identity and interval, and default/-O duplicate-baseline behavior. Original function AST extracted without importing its surrounding native preparation module.
new_gate.added_cycles_compatibility: Retains observation_id, reference_side, start_s and end_s. Source interval fields must be finite, constant across all 150 rows, with end greater than start.
